CARBORUNDUM UNIVERSAL | PRODUCT PORTFOLIO

Company Overview
- Murugappa Group company founded in 1954.
- Headquartered in Chennai, India.
- Mines-to-market advanced materials company.
- Offers 20,000+ product variants.
- Core areas include abrasives and ceramics.
- Also operates in refractories and electrominerals.

Bonded Abrasives
- Products include vitrified and resin wheels.
- Also offers rubber and precision wheels.
- Applications include grinding and metal cutting.
- Serves auto, bearings and aerospace industries.
- Also serves steel and engineering industries.

Coated Abrasives
- Products include belts, sheets and rolls.
- Also offers flap and fibre discs.
- Used for sanding and polishing.
- Supports weld blending and rust removal.
- Serves woodworking and fabrication industries.

Non-Woven Abrasives
- Products include hand pads and rolls.
- Also manufactures non-woven wheels.
- Used for cleaning and blending.
- Enables fine finishing without deep scratches.
- Suitable for contour finishing applications.

Super Abrasives
- Products include diamond and CBN wheels.
- Used for grinding hard materials.
- Applications include carbides and ceramics.
- Supports aerospace alloy grinding.
- Also used for turbine-blade regrinding.

Power Tools & Fluids
- Products include grinders and tile cutters.
- Also offers drills, hammers and chop saws.
- Metalworking fluids include coolants and oils.
- Supports cutting, grinding and drilling.
- Fluids provide cooling and lubrication.

Electrominerals
- Products include brown and white fused alumina.
- Also produces black and green silicon carbide.
- Portfolio includes alumina-zirconia and fused zirconia.
- Supplies raw grains for abrasives.
- Applications include refractories and thermal spraying.
- Also serves surface-treatment applications.

Super Refractories
- Products include SiC and mullite.
- Also offers high-alumina and insulating bricks.
- Portfolio includes castables and ramming masses.
- Slide-gate plates and nozzles are included.
- Used in extreme-temperature industrial environments.
- Key industries include steel and aluminium.

Industrial & Technical Ceramics
- Products include wear tiles and liners.
- Also offers metallised ceramics and grinding media.
- Ballistic plates and tiles are manufactured.
- Applications include wear and corrosion protection.
- Serves mining, power and defence industries.
- Also supports electronics applications.

Corrosion Protection
- ProDORiTE offers chemical-resistant linings.
- Also provides protective coatings.
- GFRP and CFRP composites are available.
- Protects concrete and steel structures.
- Applications include tanks and chemical plants.
- Also serves water and sewage infrastructure.

Ceramic Fibres
- Products include refractory fibre blankets.
- Also offers boards and papers.
- Bio-soluble fibre is part of portfolio.
- Provides high-temperature insulation.
- Used around furnaces and kilns.
- Serves glass, steel and energy industries.

KEY TAKEAWAY
CUMI operates a highly diversified materials platform spanning abrasives, electrominerals, refractories, technical ceramics, corrosion protection and ceramic fibres, serving multiple industrial and high-temperature applications.

What regulators see that investors often ignore 👇

Every time a regulator acts, investors first ask: "How much EPS gets hit?" Regulators ask something else: "Is the market structure fair for the end consumer?" That's a very different lens. 
Thoughts on recent #PBFintech & older #IEX n more

Case in point: Recent change on insurance commissions. The proposed changes effectively aim to reduce distribution costs & curb excessive upfront payouts on some products. Investors see lower margins. Regulators see lower customer acquisition costs & better value for policyholders.

Truth is, hardly anyone argues that insurance has zero mis-selling. Higher upfront commissions have often created incentives to sell what pays the most, not what suits the customer best. If that problem exists, intervention shouldn't be surprising.

The irony is that many investors celebrate efficiency in every industry except their own portfolio holdings. When a regulator targets excess distribution costs, the reaction is often outrage instead of introspection.

Look at insurance expense ratios. Even as the industry scaled up, commission/expense pools as a % of premium remained elevated in several segments. The regulator's job is to ask: why isn't scale translating into lower customer costs?

Learning from MFs TER. Every TER cut was seen as fatal attack. Prediction was: growth will die, distributors will vanish, profit collapse. Instead industry adapted. Players became efficient, direct plans gained share, technology reduced costs, investor participation & AUM surged

Market coupling in power exch. Investors focus: which exchange lose market share. Regulators focus: consumers get better price discovery. Market coupling means bids/orders from all exch get pooled to discover a single price. One price improves efficiency & reduces fragmentation

Could one exchange lose moat? Maybe. But from system perspective, better price discovery, deeper liquidity & lower market distortion are hard to ignore.
Regulators rarely optimize for shareholder returns. They optimize for consumers, market efficiency & long-term public interest

Think about hospitals. If tomorrow there is stricter price regulation, hospital stocks may get hit. As investors we'd feel the pain. But can anyone honestly deny healthcare costs are becoming unaffordable for a large section of Indians?
One may argue India's healthcare is still cheaper than many countries. True. But the person comparing prices globally is not the same person struggling to pay a hospital bill locally.

Markets often assume regulators must protect industry profitability. Regulators believe industries shouldn't fleece poor customers. When public benefit & industry profits collide, the regulator's choice is usually obvious.

That's why stock market reaction is often the last variable in the regulator's decision. If a policy improves consumer outcomes, transparency, affordability or efficiency, temporary shareholder pain rarely changes the outcome.

Cupid Limited  Converts up to 30 Lakh Baazar Style Warrants into Equity Shares

Cupid Limited has approved the conversion of up to 30 lakh warrants of Baazar Style Retail Limited into an equivalent number of equity shares at a fixed price of ₹328.25 per share.

Warrant Details:
* In January 2026, Cupid approved investment in 1.01 crore warrants of Baazar Style at ₹328.25 per warrant.
* 15 lakh warrants were already converted into equity shares on May 15,  2026, leaving 86 lakh warrants were outstanding.
* Cupid now proposes to convert up to 30 lakh warrants in one or more tranches.
* If the full 30 lakh warrants are converted, 56 lakh warrants will remain outstanding.
* The proposed conversion will involve an investment of approximately ₹73.86 crore.

 Business Impact:
The investment is aimed at strengthening Cupid’s retail presence and expanding the reach of its FMCG product portfolio. Baazar Style currently operates 283+ stores and plans to grow to 500+ stores over the next 3 years, providing a larger platform for Cupid’s products and expanding their consumer reach, visibility and availability.

HBL ENGINEERING | PLT + KAVACH + EDT + FUSES 🚀

PLT Battery Demand
- PLT battery demand is very strong.
- Data centers are driving significant demand.
- Current capacity is insufficient for demand.
- PLT capacity will increase by 50%.
- Further capex may be required next year.
- Defence and aerospace are additional applications.
- Volumes remain relatively low in these segments.

Key Growth Segments
- Kavach remains a major opportunity.
- EDT is another key growth segment.
- Fuses provide significant long-term potential.
- These three segments could drive growth.
- Management expects strong opportunity over coming years.

Fuse Business
- Fuse business has built-in entry barriers.
- HBL is already generating fuse revenues.
- Revenue is expected to grow further.
- Management sees potential for J-curve growth.
- Growth could accelerate over next 2–3 fiscals.
- High entry barriers support competitive positioning.

Kavach Opportunity
- Competition remains a market concern.
- Management expects eventual dominance by top players.
- Railway interoperability favours fewer major suppliers.
- Some existing players could eventually exit.
- HBL remains positioned within the opportunity.

Electronics Supply Chain
- Key component supply was disrupted recently.
- Impact was visible over the last six months.
- Strong demand has partly offset supply constraints.
- Pricing could normalise over coming quarters.
- Near-term margin pressure cannot be ruled out.

EDT Opportunity
- Government focus on heavy-truck electrification is increasing.
- Objective includes reducing pollution and fuel costs.
- HBL is focusing on EDT rather than trucks.
- EDT means Electric Drive Train.
- Some trucks will be built for POC.
- HBL sees EDT as a core-kit opportunity.

EDT Commercialisation
- EDT development has faced delays.
- Further commercialisation delays remain possible.
- Product marketing strategy is still being evaluated.
- Multiple market segments are being assessed.
- Company will target the most suitable segment.
- Profitability will influence final market selection.

Indigenous EDT Capability
- Management says no Indian company currently offers similar indigenous EDTs.
- HBL aims for an internally developed solution.
- Segment reportedly has no supply-chain dependency.
- Indigenous technology can support strategic positioning.

Maritime Adjacency
- EDT technology can extend into maritime propulsion.
- Applications include boats and tugs.
- Ships also provide potential applications.
- Maritime sector is seeing government support.
- Water-metro adoption supports future opportunities.
- Kochi model could be replicated elsewhere.
- Varanasi is among potential expansion markets.

Cochin Shipyard JV
- JV opportunity extends beyond Cochin Shipyard.
- Products can potentially address export markets.
- Management considers current products exportable.
- Export opportunities could expand the addressable market.

Management & Guidance
- Succession planning remains decentralised in approach.
- Concrete succession details are yet to emerge.
- No specific FY30 revenue guidance provided.
- Management indicated FY30 could be much better.
- Detailed guidance may come later.

KEY TAKEAWAY 🎯
HBL's growth pipeline increasingly spans PLT batteries, Kavach, fuses and EDT, with data-center demand supporting PLT while indigenous EDT and maritime applications provide longer-term optionality.

SEDEMAC | ENGINE CONTROLLERS + EV SOFTWARE 🚀

Software Is The Moat

- Controllers manage engines, generators and motors.
- Software determines operating speed and response.
- Software controls generator starting behaviour.
- Algorithms respond to heat and load.
- Customer approvals create switching barriers.
- Retesting alternatives requires time and money.
- Company holds 12 technology patents.

Strong Market Position
- SEDEMAC dominates generator controller applications.
- Holds ~75% Indian generator market share.
- Holds ~14% global generator market share.
- Supplies engine controllers to major customers.
- Covers ~35% Indian 2W/3W market.
- Over 80% new ISG chip growth came from SEDEMAC.

FY26 Financial Performance
- FY26 revenue reached ₹1,058 Cr.
- Revenue grew 61% YoY.
- Controller sales approached 4 million units.
- Lifetime controller sales crossed 12 million units.
- Company is now almost debt-free.
- Capital efficiency remains strong.
- ROCE is around 40%.

EV Controller Breakthrough
- EV controller revenue reached ₹68 Cr in FY26.
- Previous-year EV controller revenue was ₹10 Cr.
- Revenue increased nearly sevenfold.
- Around 1 million electric 3W controllers deployed.
- Deployment took 28 quarters.
- EV 2W opportunity is growing rapidly.
- Existing manufacturing base supports expansion.

Existing Business Funds EV Growth
- Generator business remains a major cash generator.
- Engine controllers remain another core business.
- Cash flows support EV controller investments.
- Same factory can support multiple product lines.
- Existing customer relationships provide distribution leverage.

Q1 FY27 Momentum
- Q1 FY27 profits nearly doubled YoY.
- Growth indicates continued operating momentum.
- Generator business continues generating cash.
- EV investments remain a key growth focus.

EV Growth Opportunity
- 2W and 3W electrification expands addressable market.
- Controller demand increases with EV adoption.
- Existing 3W penetration provides a strong base.
- 2W EV growth offers another opportunity.
- Software expertise can support new applications.

KEY TAKEAWAY 🎯
SEDEMAC's core advantage lies in proprietary control software, customer qualification and installed base. Generator cash flows are funding a rapidly expanding EV controller business, creating a transition from conventional engines toward electric mobility.

Carbon steel is 70% of Shyam Metalics' revenue today. On management's FY31 roadmap it drops to well under half.

Stainless steel takes the other side of that trade, 7% to 28% of revenue. Auto-grade SBQ bar and railway wagons, both nil today, fill most of the rest. Ferro alloys, the highest-margin line now, shrink to a rounding error.

The point of the move: the same ore and power base, sold as engineered products on contract instead of as commodity steel on daily prices. Stainless already realises roughly 4x per tonne what carbon steel does.

It's a roadmap where the destination is a stainless, auto-grade and rolling-stock company, not a sponge-iron-and-TMT one.

Why would Interarch spend ₹80 cr on new capacity when its existing plants run at just 70%? 

Two filings from yesterday answer it together.

The Reg 30 disclosure: 24,000 MTPA added at Attivaram, AP, installed capacity up from 2.21 to 2.45 lakh MT, funded from internal accruals, commercial production from 24 Sep.

The press release: this is not PEB. It is a heavy structural steel plant making large hot-rolled sections and plate girders for high-rise, data centers, semicon fabs and heavy industrial projects. Spare PEB capacity simply cannot do this work.

So the 70% isn't a red flag. The old lines are free, but they can't make this product. That's also why this plant cost ~2.5x more per tonne than the PEB line next door: heavier machines for heavier work. And Phase 2 is already being built

India’s power sector is moving towards a much more flexible electricity market. ⚡️

• Draft National Electricity Policy proposes customised power arrangements for data centres & green hydrogen projects, including greater flexibility in electricity usage and storage.

• Renewable energy already accounts for ~37% of installed capacity, while by 2047, 80%+ of capacity could come from non-fossil sources.

• This makes battery storage and grid balancing increasingly critical. Battery storage costs have fallen from ~₹10/unit in 2023 to below ₹4/unit.

• CEA estimates nearly ₹5.8 lakh crore investment in battery storage could be required through 2035-36.

• We are already seeing the impact of renewable volatility - spot power prices recently crashed from ₹10/unit to just 1 paisa within hours.

India won't just need more power generation. It will need storage, transmission, grid management and demand flexibility to make renewable energy reliable at scale.

This could create a much larger opportunity across the BESS, power equipment, transmission and energy-management ecosystem.

ORACLE'S DATACENTER 'FORCE MAJEURE'

Impact here: Oracle -> Bloom -> MTAR Tech

Oracle was -4% & Bloom was -3%.

What has happened -> Oracle sent a “force majeure” notice to the builders of its Project Jupiter future datacenter in New Mexico.

Project Jupiter is a 4-building campus in New Mexico - roughly 1,400 acres outside El Paso. OpenAI is the primary Oracle customer for the site. Power was expected to be delivered via Bloom Energy fuel cells which would be fueled with natural gas.

The Green Chile Project pipeline - a 17-mile gas pipeline being built by Energy Transfer to supply the site - has been delayed from August 2026 to February 2027.

The delay follows repeated refusals by the New Mexico State Land Office to grant right-of-way permits across state-owned trust land. Local officials & environmental groups have opposed the project, citing concerns about climate impact and use of natural resources.

Bloom needs that gas supply in order to start commissioning at the site. 

The 2.5 GW associated with Project Jupiter is the largest deployment in Bloom’s disclosed pipeline against its backlog.

Chinese Competition

- Management expects healthy market competition.
- Competition can pressure turbine pricing.
- Suzlon remains focused on domestic execution.

- Fabs consume ultra-high-purity materials.
- Electronic gases are critical inputs.
- Key chemicals include HCl, HF and H₂SO₄.
- H₂O₂, IPA and solvents support processing.
- Fluorochemicals serve specialised semiconductor applications.
- Photoresists enable advanced lithography processes.
- Resins and polymers support semiconductor manufacturing.
- CMP materials enable wafer surface polishing.

Fab + Packaging + Testing
- CG Power is building semiconductor capabilities.
- Kaynes Technology is expanding semiconductor operations.

- Packaging and testing are critical ecosystem layers.

Design + Engineering
- MosChip operates in semiconductor design services.

Complete Value Chain
- Silicon forms the core foundation.
- Chemicals enable wafer processing.
- Electronic gases support manufacturing processes.
- Photoresists enable lithography.
- Wafers undergo fabrication and processing.
- CMP enables precision surface finishing.
- Etching removes selected material layers.
- Deposition builds semiconductor layers.
- Lithography defines circuit patterns.
- Packaging protects and connects chips.
- Testing validates chip performance.
- Substrates and PCBs support integration.
- Thermal management handles generated heat.
- Electronics represent the final application layer.

KEY TAKEAWAY 🎯
India's semiconductor opportunity extends beyond fabs, OSAT and chip design. Chemicals, gases, equipment, packaging, testing, substrates and thermal management create a much broader ecosystem.

Moving from making chemicals for others to inventing your own puts PI in different territory among Indian agrochemical firms

Pioxaniliprole belongs to diamide family of insecticides. Diamides are among most widely used insect control chemicals in farming, with $3 billion in global sales. Biggest diamide product, chlorantraniliprole, once earned $1.8 billion per year for FMC before its patent expired in 2022. 

After patent expiry, Chinese generic makers entered at 40 to 60% lower prices. PI Industries is entering this same $3 billion market but with its own patent, not as generic maker. 

Owning intellectual property means PI sets its own prices and keeps much larger share of revenue.

PI Industries has been making crop protection chemicals for global companies on contract for years that means PI manufactures what others invent and earns manufacturing margins. 

Pioxaniliprole changes that picture from scratch. PI invented this molecule itself and filed patent applications covering it worldwide in 2019 and 2022. Government has already cleared technical material for export. This means PI can sell Pioxaniliprole in other countries, license it to partners and collect royalties. 

Going from manufacturing for others to owning your own chemistry is different business with much higher earnings potential

India ships $6 billion worth of crop protection chemicals every year but has never invented its own insecticide that got government approval. Every patented insecticide used by Indian farmers was invented by foreign companies like Syngenta, Bayer or FMC. 

PI Industries just broke that pattern. Registration committee formally recorded Pioxaniliprole as first insecticide active ingredient discovered in India. PI now holds 250 plus patents and 90 plus molecules in R&D pipeline.

text:
Tata Group Boardroom Tug of War
Some history repeat; Some history rhyme
30 yrs ago it was Ratan Tata vs Russi Mody. Today, many see shades of that battle in the Chandra vs Noel Tata face-off
Back in the 1990s, Ratan Tata was consolidating authority within a sprawling Tata empire run by powerful Operating entity heads. Russi Mody was among the most influential Tata executives of his era. Larger-than-life personality, huge public profile & massive influence within the group.
Ratan Tata believed Tata Group needed one strategic centre of gravity. Not multiple power centres running individual fiefdoms. Eventually, Russi Mody exited & Ratan Tata tightened control over the conglomerate.
Fast forward three decades.
The debate is again centred around leadership, control & the future direction of Tata Sons. This time its Noel Tata, who chairs Tata Trusts, & N Chandrasekaran, who leads Tata Sons
Key contentions are Chandra’s reappointment as chairman & Tata Sons listing. Noel Tata has opposed both
The striking part? Tata Sons board backed Chandra by a 4:1 vote, while Noel Tata stood opposed
Russi Mody took the battle public. Media interviews, public sparring & headline-grabbing exchanges became part of the story.
Chandra, however, has largely stayed silent in public
Whether history repeats or merely echoes, one thing is clear
Generational change of Tata leadership eventually confronts the same question.

Is India investing enough for future capacity

India is usually described as a consumption economy. Consumption contributes >60% of GDP. But the story becomes incomplete when we ignore what's happening on the investment side and other aspects of our economy

India's Gross Capital Formation is ~32.6% of GDP. Lower than China's ~40%, but China's per capita GDP is several times of India's. Comparing ratios without considering income levels misses the context.

A developing country cannot allocate every ₹ toward factories & infra. A large share of resources must also support the bottom of the pyramid through housing, healthcare, education & welfare.

A harmonious society requires a minimum standard of living for those at the bottom. India is building capacity while simultaneously funding social stability. That's a tougher balancing act than many realize.

So let's move beyond GDP narratives & look at hard physical data. India's share of global GDP is only ~3.5% yet produces roughly 10% of the world's steel. Steel almost 3x our weight in global GDP. Steel isn't consumed for consumption's sake, but goes into factories, rail tracks, power plants, ports, airports, infrastructure etc

Cement tells the same story. India produces ~400 MT annually out of ~4,000 MT globally. Again, roughly 10% global share despite only ~3.5% share of world GDP. Countries don't consume steel & cement at this scale unless they are building physical assets. These are the raw materials of future GDP.

Power generation presents a slightly different picture. India's share of global electricity output is lower than steel & cement, but still materially ahead of its global GDP share. India with 1800bn units vs 32,000bn units, 6% global share

The evidence suggests India is investing for future capability. One may argue the investment cycle started later than it should have, but the direction is unmistakable. Steel, Cement & Power share point toward economy preparing for a much larger future.

The scale of projects are also changing. DFCs, industrial corridors, semiconductor fabs, renewable energy parks, metros, airports, transmission corridors & logistics networks are larger than anything India attempted before.

If this trend continues, India's share of global steel, cement & power usage is likely to keep rising. Higher material intensity today is often a precursor to higher economic output tomorrow.

Maybe the better way to describe India isn't "consumption economy." It's a country simultaneously consuming, uplifting millions & building future productive capacity. 
India need a balancing act of Building future and taking care of the needy, which it is working towards

For more such views, follow
https://x.com/RaviBhandari83
Flex working space thematic report

De-Dollarization lets peek into central bank reserves

Central banks are diversifying but US$ isn't giving up the throne anytime soon. Headlines scream de-dollarization bt US$ still makes up ~57% of global FX reserves. That's down from decades ago, but still miles ahead of everyone else.

Euro is the 2nd largest reserve currency at ~20%. But Europe faces weak growth, aging demographics, fiscal stress & fragmented politics. Hence no comfort for people looking to diversify away from US$

Then its China. Despite its economic size, RMB is only ~2% of global reserves & ~2% of global payments. Clear reflection of trust issues with the dragon. deep capital markets, convertibility & rule of law issues also there

They're moving into something with no issuer at all: Gold. Central banks themselves are now one of the biggest sources of gold demand globally, roughly buy ~30% of annual global mine production

Gold isn't rising only because investors are bullish. Significant chunk of global prodn is locked away by sovereign balance sheets. In 2026, central banks gold buying at slower pace vs 2025 due to 60% price rise.

Among the Major buyers were Poland, China, Brazil, India etc. 
Then there are few sellers too. Turkey has been among the largest sellers this year, reportedly selling ~83t YTD to support liquidity & FX/US$ needs.

That’s the problem. Though world want to move away from US$ in the long term but  issue in the medium term created due to lack of US$ in the country. 
Case in point Turkiye

Russia has also been a notable seller, reducing reserves by ~44t YTD as it seeks hard-currency liquidity. But Russia is also large producer of Gold

Gold is becoming a reserve diversification asset in a world where trust in fiat issuers is fragmenting.
BUT de-dollarization in reserves doesn't mean de-dollarization in trade.
That’s two very different thing

Global trade still run on the USD infrastructure. That network effect is incredibly hard to replace.
So its two-step process. Trade continues in USD.
But exporting nations convert a portion of their accumulated surplus reserves into gold, commodities, sovereign funds or other reserve assets.

The world may keep transacting in dollars while increasingly choosing not to store all its savings in dollars.

Conclusion:
Real story is different from "the end of the USD."
Reserve diversification is real.
Dollar replacement is not. Not in near future

Birla trying to replicate Paint like disruption in Wire & Cables
India's W&C industry is a INR 1.1trn & growing at ~13% CAGR. Despite its size (0.3% of India GDP), industry remains fragmented with top 6 players control ~50% share

Market is roughly split into 3 equal buckets: Wires, LT Cables & MV/HT/EHV/Specialized Cables. Cables compared to wire is more organized, house wires have larger unorganized participation. Overall unorganized is > 30%

what attracted Birla. W&C sits at the intersection of electrification, urbanization & digitization. Housing, infra, renewables, data centres & manufacturing all need more wires.

Ultratech has launched Ultravolt with planned capex of ₹18 bn. Initial plant capacity has already started production ahead of schedule at Bharuch. The market compares this with the paint disruption. Lets look at numbers

Grasim's paint capex was ~65-70% of Asian Paint. Ultravolt's ₹18 bn capex is 30% of Polycab gross block. Plus, Polycab's gross block is expected to reach ~₹94 bn in FY28 while KEI could reach ~₹43 bn. Ultravolt's announced gross block is only ₹18 bn

The biggest advantage for Ultratech is raw material availability. Copper & Aluminium dominate industry economics and the Birla ecosystem already has deep expertise & inhouse production

Demand-intelligence advantage. Cement is purchased 6 months before wires in building construction. Ultratech can potentially spot demand trends 4-6 months ahead of competitors

Builder relationships, contractor network & Ultratech Building Solutions outlets create a ready-made ecosystem for cross-selling wires. That's a powerful advantage most new entrant

Ultravolt has prepared well. Better channel incentives, faster delivery commitments, aggressive marketing & strong retailer engagement are already creating buzz. But replicating the paint playbook won't be straightforward. 

Paints & cement share significant overlap in distribution. Wires are largely sold through electrical dealers, distributors, retailers & electrician networks. Building an electrical distribution franchise takes years

Another key difference is profitability. Leading W&C players operate at ~12-14% EBITDA margins, far lower than the 18-20%+ margins paint Co. enjoyed before disruption. With lower margins, room for aggressive pricing is limited

Further: Utility, industrial, railway, transmission & infra projects require extensive testing, approvals, certifications & execution history before meaningful scale can be achieved.
Conclusion: Birla has genuine advantage in raw material sourcing, builder relationships & demand visibility. But unlike paints, incumbents start with lower margins, stronger technical moats & entrenched distribution

Jury is still out. Ultravolt looks prepared. Space will remain interesting

Coforge Chairman resignation : Lets dig deeper

OP Bhatt's resignation came after disagreements around the Board evaluation process. In his resignation note, he says continuing on Board amid differences regarding his "good faith actions" would not be conducive to Board effective functioning 

OP Bhatt is not a conventional IT industry chairman. He is among India's most respected bankers, having led SBI between 2006-11 & later served on boards across large corporates including Tata Group companies

The market doesn’t take such update kindly, but Bhatt's continuation was already under question even before the resignation. Shareholders (inc largest shareholder Advent) voted against his reappointment as Independent Director from May'27
 
Let’s go a bit in history: The company was earlier known as NIIT Tech before its ownership transition & eventual rebranding to Coforge. Barings acquired control of NIIT in 2020, leading to ownership change then.

Later, Barings steadily monetised its stake through multiple block deals as the company scaled in size, profitability & market value. After Barings' complete exit by FY24, Co. become fully public market institutional owned.

OP Bhatt joined the board in 2024 & became Chairman during a phase when Coforge was pursuing aggressive scale-up ambitions. Coforge accelerated inorganic growth. The acquisition of Cigniti significantly expanded its engineering & digital capabilities under him.

The much bigger acquisition Encora was also under OP Bhatt. The acquisition materially increased Coforge's scale, global delivery footprint & exposure to high-growth digital engineering segments.

Encora also changed the shareholding landscape. Through the transaction, Advent became the largest shareholder in Coforge, making its views impossible for the board to ignore. That's why the key takeaway may not be the resignation itself. The bigger story could be that the largest shareholder & the Chairman were not aligned on important matters. 

The bullish view is that management execution remains intact. The cautious view is that whenever Chairman, Board & largest shareholder are not on the same page, governance questions emerge and mgmt. energy is focussed away from growth.

Impact of change in EV subsidy policy from 31 July 2026

PM E-DRIVE subsidy for electric 2Ws ended on 31 Jul 2026. Govt earlier plan was to support E2W till 31 Mar 2026, then gave the industry a 4-month extension till Jul-end as there was unutilized budget

PM E-DRIVE replaced FAME-II in Oct'24 with a 10,900 Cr outlay. The idea was simple: help EV adoption scale while supporting charging infra, buses, trucks & other EV segments

initially, e-2W buyers got subsidy of 5,000/kWh, capped at 10,000/ vehicle. That was a meaningful discount for mass-market scooters. From Apr'25, cut by half to 2,500/kWh with max capped at 5,000/Veh. Signalling gradual withdrawal of support.

Now for 2W, even that 5,000 support is gone. Effective acquisition cost of an EV scooter will move up. 5,000 price hike may not sound huge, but in entry-level its imp for price-sensitive consumer

Some moderation in electric 2W demand was expected. OEMs were preparing for it as subsidy-led growth gradually transitions to product-led growth. 

August EV 2W market share came lower than July. E2W MS has come down but not in 3w as July subsidy withdrawal only 2W not in 3W. August is typically a non-festival month & seasonality also matters. OEMs should absorb subsidy via better exchange / financing offers

Market is also looking for next phase of EV support. Discussions around "FAME III" continue, but indications suggest focus could shift towards vehicle other than 2W. 2W penetration already >10% while other segment need more support

If electric 2Ws are eventually excluded from future demand subsidies, industry economics will increasingly depend on product quality, distribution, service network & battery costs instead of govt incentives.

One factor often ignored: OEMs capacity are planned in a way where capacity expansion will happen in same facility. Hence, incremental capex intensity will be far lower. Gradual drivetrain shift will continue without large incremental capex

Bottom line: Subsidy withdrawal may create short-term demand noise, but the long-term story remains the same. India's 2W market is enormous, EV penetration is still low, and the migration from ICE to EV is likely to be a long, gradual journey rather than a subsidy-driven sprint.

**FCNR Sugar Rush What does it means for India**
FCNR experiment has turned into a blockbuster. Total inflows exceeded $136bn vs market expectations of ~$80bn. FCNR(B) deposits alone ~$127bn
  
Like Hindi movie, climax was amazing. 
Total inflows were ~$41bn by July-end, ~$73bn by Aug 21 and ~$136bn by Aug 31. Biggest forex mobilization drives India has ever seen. August was where the real frenzy happened. FCNR deposits jumped from ~$65.4bn on Aug 21 to ~$127.2bn by Aug 31.
  
Why did NRIs rush in? RBI effectively removed the pain point: currency hedging cost. Banks offered attractive yields while RBI absorbed swap costs For investors, FCNR became a rare risk-reward opportunity. Attractive $ returns + ability to leverage deposits (leverage run 4-5x)
  
FCNR nuance: Depositor takes bank credit risk but avoids INR depreciation risk since deposits remain in foreign currency. Currency mismatch is largely handled by RBI A key incentive for banks: incremental FCNR funds were exempted from CRR & SLR requirements.
  
More deployable money, less regulatory drag hence higher NIMs, Every $ mobilized can potentially earn better spreads for banks Flip side: Liquidity is now overflowing. System liquidity has surged sharply as these inflows entered the banking system

When banks are flush with money, appetite for wholesale funding drops. That's already showing up in lower CD rates & softer short-term funding costs Excess liquidity usually pushes overnight money market rates lower. Too much cash chasing too few opportunities compress yields
 
The RBI also gets a strategic advantage. Larger forex reserves and dollar balances improve its ability to manage forward market positions & reduce pressure from speculative USD demand. Forward dollar short should be reduced going forward
 
For currency speculator, the message is important. Betting aggressively against ₹ becomes tougher when RBI has significantly larger forex ammunition and stronger external buffers Now comes the hard part. Raising $136bn is the easy part.
  
Deploying it productively is the challenge. These are time-bound liabilities with an embedded cost. Eventually the money must earn more than it costs. INR already showing strength: USDINR below 95 today
 
The success of this scheme won't be judged by the $136bn raised. It will be judged by whether India converts this liquidity windfall into stronger growth, stable ₹, lower funding stress & productive credit creation over the next few years

Is Pvt Banks Really Losing Share vs PSU Banks?

Everyone is talking about PSU banks taking share from Pvt banks. The narrative is simple: PSU banks are growing faster than Pvt banks, so PSU banks are winning. But the reality is a lot more nuanced.

Argument is : PSU banks are fine with 1.0-1.3% RoA vs  Pvt banks target higher profitability. Pvt banks don't want to trade-off profitability for growth.

This has impacted valuations. Premium Pvt bank multiples came with expectation of steadily MS gain vs PSU. Post-Covid, that trend has slowed, creating doubts.

If PSU banks are sacrificing yield for growth, where should it show up first? HFC, safest retail assets with low NPA, Yet PSU bank share has drifted from ~35% in FY21 to ~34% in H1FY26, while Pvt banks have inched up from ~39% to ~40%.

If PSU banks were aggressively chasing growth regardless of return, housing should have been the biggest battleground. The data doesn't show that. PSU gained initially, now plateaued. 

PSU not gainin share from Pvt banks. Market share remained stable, data also inc. HDFC merger boost for pvt bank

So where is PSU growth actually coming from? A large part is Gold Loans.

Many Pvt banks have stayed away from becoming aggressive gold lenders. The business is operationally intensive and risky. PSU banks have been far more active, esp Canara/SBIN. 

Recently, incremental industry gold loan growth has come primarily from PSU banks, increasing their dominance in banking gold-loan AUM.

Second area is Agri lending. PSU banks have stepped up agri lending. May be it’s mandate-driven, or due to deeper reach into semi-urban and rural India where Agri credit demand is.
These segments Pvt banks is not that agressive. PSU banks are gaining share at the system level. But pvt dominance continue in safe mortgages, affluent retail.

Jefferies power equipment

Many Problem: Solar led grid instability / Energy import / Pollution One solution: EV India is winning solar race. Solar supply a huge chunk of daytime power, pushing net grid demand sharply lower arnd noon. But demand peaks after sunset. That's the classic "duck curve" problem

~80 GW swing created largely by renewable output. The irony: clean power is available when demand isn't. Several states doing solar curtailment as the grid couldn't absorb all midday generation. So, next phase of green transition is tougher than just adding more solar panels

India imports ~90% of its crude oil needs & roughly half of its natural gas . Energy security remains one of the biggest economic vulnerabilities. Crude oil is among India's largest import items. Every $ oil prices widens the import bill = trade deficit = pressure on Rupee

Air pollution remains a public health emergency in major metros. Delhi frequently records PM2.5 levels many multiples above WHO norms, while Mumbai too has seen worsening air quality episodes. Solar, oil imports & air pollution are not separate challenges. They are connected

The common link is urban transport. A large share of oil consumption in metros comes from ICE cars commuting daily between home & office. Think about office parking lots. Vehicles remain parked for 8-10 hrs during the exact period when solar generation is highest

What if every major office complex became a daytime EV charging hub? Cars would consume power when solar generation is abundant, helping flatten the duck curve instead of deepening it.

Corp can accelerate this shift. EV subsidy for employees & workplace chargin infra can become part of CSR spend (2% of PBT) Vehicles in metros spend most working hours parked at offices. Converting 20%+ of parking capacity into chargers can create a daytime demand for solar power

One solution. Multiple benefits. More EVs = lower oil imports, cleaner city air, higher daytime power consumption, better solar utilisation & stable grid. Sometimes the smartest energy storage isn't a battery plant. It's millions of parked EVs connected to chargers.
